compiled_state.title: fix-bug recurrence prevention: tree-wide antipattern scan and hermetic repro
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

Pattern 3 (identical-root-cause regressions, ~10% of recent fixes) is the dominant repeat-bug class: the same defect is fixed in one script and rediscovered in another months later. /dso:fix-bug mandates intent-search for the failing ticket's own history but does not require a tree-wide scan for the same antipattern after a fix lands, and the prior-art protocol (prior-art-search.md:79-88) explicitly excludes single-file fixes — exactly where Pattern 3 manifests. Separately, RED tests are not required to reproduce in a clean environment, so a fix verified against a shell contaminated by an inherited environment passes locally and re-breaks in CI (Pattern 1). DSO maintainers and the fix-bug agent itself pay for the same bug two, three, or four times.

This epic adds two complementary fix-bug discipline additions: (1) a tree-wide antipattern scan after every fix, with the surfaced query promotable to the known-antipatterns registry delivered by epic 7575-5a90; and (2) a hermetic-repro requirement for the shell/bash RED test in fix-bug Phase E Step 1.

## Cited evidence

Pattern 3 recurrence chain (the empirical proof):
- 09d8-11f0 (commit e913a71d5a) — pre-commit-format-fix.sh: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT under set -u
- fe45-0b58 (commit dcbe98f3ef) — skip-review-check.sh, same root cause two months later; ticket explicitly cites 09d8-11f0
- 82ad-7bb3 (commit f5a055d1fa) — bash-runner.sh, same root cause again
- 97a7-4504 (commit 495c8c4b4f) — annotation follow-up on bash-runner.sh, same root cause
- Each ticket was treated as a single-file fix and excluded from prior-art search by the prior-art-search.md:79-88 routine-exclusions rule.

Hermeticity (G9): Pattern 1 bugs (fe45-0b58, 09d8-11f0, 82ad-7bb3) were caught by CI in a partially hermetic environment, "fixed" against a contaminated local environment, then re-broken by subsequent changes. A hermetic-repro requirement at fix-bug time would have surfaced the contamination immediately.

## Approach

Additive gates inside /dso:fix-bug. Phase G's existing anti-pattern-scan.md sub-agent is extended to emit two required SCAN_RESULT fields — query_used (the exact grep/sg pattern executed) and trailer_line ("Antipattern-Scan: <query> root=<repo-root> matches=<n>"); the orchestrator copies trailer_line verbatim into the commit message rather than hand-constructing it (a missing field makes SCAN_RESULT malformed and fails the step). A new helper plugins/dso/hooks/check-antipattern-scan-trailer.sh performs the commit-gate check, invoked from a HARD-GATE in fix-bug's commit step (skill-internal — not a global COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md gate, since ~9 skills consume that workflow). The hermetic recipe is encapsulated in a new helper plugins/dso/scripts/run-hermetic.sh so the contaminant-clearing idiom is never transcribed inline. The bug-type-<slug> classification (epic 4911, shipped) is consumed only at retro time for recurrence aggregation — there is no coupling between the classifier and the antipattern scan.

## Success Criteria

1. A /dso:fix-bug run that fixes a shell-script bug emits an "Antipattern-Scan: <query> root=<scan-root> matches=<n>" commit trailer, produced as the trailer_line field of the anti-pattern-scan.md SCAN_RESULT and copied verbatim into the commit message. The root field records the scan root, evidencing tree-wide scope.

2. plugins/dso/hooks/check-antipattern-scan-trailer.sh, invoked from a HARD-GATE in fix-bug's commit step, refuses to complete the commit when the Antipattern-Scan trailer is absent, or when it reports matches>0 without a machine-verifiable follow-up artifact per match. Valid artifacts are exhaustively: (a) a ticket ID returned by `dso ticket create` recorded in the trailer; (b) the match file also appearing in git diff (pulled into scope); (c) a "# antipattern-ok: <reason>" annotation at the match line where <reason> is one of {different-context, dead-code, already-tracked:<id>}, capped at 3 annotations per session without an explicit user-approval dialog. The gate applies to every commit authored within a fix-bug invocation, including Phase G's anti-pattern fix sub-agents; commits from independent skills (sprint, debug-everything) are never gated because they never invoke this step.

3. A shell/bash RED test that does not reproduce under plugins/dso/scripts/run-hermetic.sh (which runs `env -u CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT bash -c 'unset "${!BASH_FUNC_@}" 2>/dev/null; <test command>'`, preserving PATH and venv) triggers a HARD-GATE full stop: fix implementation does not proceed; the bug ticket records a "Hermetic reproduction failed" comment and investigation restarts at Phase C. A test is shell/bash if and only if (a) its file ends in .sh, or (b) the resolved $TEST_CMD runner starts with bash or sh; all other cases are non-shell runners, which emit a machine-checkable "HERMETIC_SKIP: runner=<runner> reason=non-shell" token and are never blocked.

4. Phase G includes a promote-query sub-step. The known-antipatterns.yaml file and its append schema are owned by epic 7575-5a90 (consumed, not defined here). When the file exists the sub-step appends the query per that schema; when it does not, the sub-step writes a durable ticket comment "ANTIPATTERN_PROMOTE_DEFERRED: <query>" (not stdout-only), forming a backfill list for when 7575-5a90 ships.

5. A regression fixture under tests/ freezes a snapshot of the four Pattern 3 chain files (root-cause excerpts of 09d8-11f0, fe45-0b58, 82ad-7bb3, 97a7-4504) and runs the first fix's extracted query against them, asserting >=4 matches — demonstrating the tree-wide scan would have collapsed the chain into a single fix. The fixture runs deterministically in the closing session with no original environment required.

## Closure Checks

(none — all success criteria are verifiable within the closing session)

## Dependencies

- relates_to 7575-5a90 (Static-analysis defense layer) — provides known-antipatterns.yaml and check-known-antipatterns.sh. Partial-ship supported: SC1-SC3 and SC5 ship independently; SC4's promote-step degrades to a durable ANTIPATTERN_PROMOTE_DEFERRED ticket comment until the registry lands.
- relates_to 4911-c7ba (Bug-classification coverage registry, closed) — bug-type-<slug> recurrence aggregation at /dso:retro is the measurement loop this ratchet feeds; consumed at retro, not by fix-bug.

## Scenario Analysis

- Hermetic recipe must clear the contaminant, not the whole environment (critical, assumption): env -i strips PATH/venv and breaks compound test commands; the gate uses env -u plus BASH_FUNC_@ clearing while preserving the runner. Resolved in Approach + SC3.
- Exported bash functions survive env -i (high, runtime): BASH_FUNC_* exports leak through on Linux bash 4.x; run-hermetic.sh explicitly unsets them. Resolved in SC3.
- Gate keying must be skill-internal, not attribution-trailer-based (high, runtime): keying on a DSO-Skill trailer fails on local workflows (no trailer written) and on sprint-origin fix-bug sub-agents (DSO-Skill: sprint). The gate runs inside fix-bug's own commit invocation instead. Resolved in Approach + SC2.
- Anti-pattern fix-batch inter-batch commits must also be gated (high, deployment): Phase G's own fix sub-agent commits would otherwise bypass the new gates and could propagate a defective fix. SC2 explicitly includes them.
- matches=0 forgeable by a narrow scan (high, configuration): the gate cannot cryptographically verify tree-wide coverage; mitigated by recording the scan root in the trailer (SC1) and mandating repo-root scope in the Phase G procedure. Residual risk accepted: this is a discipline aid, not a proof system.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md commit/closure phase. Interaction: 0cbc-4bbb adds an in_review status + closure loop at the same phase; this epic adds a commit-time trailer check. Gate: the two compose as independent steps; neither clobbers the other's phase edits.
- Resource: fix-bug phase HARD-GATEs. Interaction: af26-dd5a makes forbidden-action HARD-GATEs load-bearing via tool-use-time enforcement. Gate: this epic's hermetic-repro and trailer gates are registered as af26-style load-bearing gates where af26 has landed.
- Resource: origin:antipattern-scan follow-up tasks. Interaction: 7271-e463 cleanup skill consumes follow-up tasks Phase G files. Gate: follow-up tickets carry a tag the cleanup skill recognizes.
- Resource: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md. Interaction: 6d90-93d5 adds Conventional-Commits format validation. Gate: trailer requirement and format validator compose without mutual rejection.
- Resource: plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml. Interaction: 7575-5a90 owns the registry; this epic appends. Gate: 7575-5a90 ships first or both coordinate on initial file creation; this epic no-ops until then.

## References

- docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md Patterns 1, 3
- docs/process-gaps-4-26.md G6, G9
- docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md G6-M1, G9-M3
- docs/new-epics-4-26.md New Epic E

### Planning Intelligence Log

- Gap analysis (Step 1): all user-named artifacts covered (fix-bug SKILL.md, /dso:commit, known-antipatterns.yaml, env-i recipe, Antipattern-Scan trailer, Pattern 3 chain). Parts executed: Part A artifact check, Part B technical self-review, Part C shared-artifact impact (found COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md consumed by ~9 skills; no fix-bug commit marker exists -> keyed gate skill-internal).
- Web research (Step 2.6): not triggered (no bright-line conditions fired — no external API, new dependency, security, novel architecture, performance, or migration signal).
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered. Scenarios surviving blue-team filter: 6 (1 critical, 5 high). All addressed in the spec (hermetic recipe correction, skill-internal keying, inter-batch gating, scan-root recording).
- Cross-epic interaction scan (Step 2.25): 134 candidate epics across 27 batches; 1 conflict (0cbc-4bbb), 1 ambiguity (af26-dd5a), 6 considerations. Practitioner chose Override + record links; relates_to links recorded to 0cbc-4bbb, af26-dd5a, 7271-e463, 6d90-93d5 (4911-c7ba and 3c01-3b89 pre-existing; 7575-5a90 reverse link already present).
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none.
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered.
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered (no external integration or first-time internal platform feature; feasibility reviewer skipped).
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: skill file modifications (fix-bug/SKILL.md). bot-psychologist dispatched; hardening recommendations folded into SC1-SC3 (artifact-extraction over self-certification, enumerated follow-up artifacts, mechanical shell classification, run-hermetic.sh helper).
- Fidelity review (Step 3): Agent Clarity 5/5 (after 1 revision cycle: self_contained 3->5), Scope 5/5/4/5, Value 5/4. All dimensions pass. Revision cycles: 1.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (no volume decision).
